en: The critically endangered Philippine eagle lays only one egg per breeding season, making its population recovery very slow.
National hero Jose Rizal could speak 22 languages, which he used to read books and translate texts from all over the world.
Before the 1987 Constitution, a Philippine president could run for re-election, but now they are strictly limited to a single six-year term.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago using only simple hand tools.
Filipino pediatrician Fe del Mundo invented a makeshift bamboo incubator that uses hot water bottles to keep premature babies warm without electricity.
The Waling-waling, known as the queen of Philippine orchids, can take up to seven years to produce its very first beautiful flower.
The Ati-Atihan festival in Aklan is known as the mother of all Philippine festivals because it inspired the Sinulog and Dinagyang.
Before the Spanish arrived, early Filipinos wrote on bamboo and leaves using Baybayin, an ancient writing system with exactly 17 characters.
The first Philippine national flag was hand-sewn in Hong Kong by Marcela Agoncillo, her daughter, and Delfina Herbosa de Natividad.
National Artist Levi Celerio wrote the lyrics for over 4,000 Philippine songs, including the famous holiday carol Ang Pasko ay Sumapit.
Filipino women won the right to vote in 1937 after an overwhelming majority of female voters said yes in a national plebiscite.
The traditional Filipino value of Bayanihan originally involved an entire community physically carrying a whole nipa hut to a new location.
